name: Moldo-Ashuu Pass
near: There are no permanent villages by the pass. From the south the road runs through the canyon of the Kurtka River from Ak-Talaa District (the district centre is Baetov); per Asia for Adventure and Kyrgyz Guide, the stretch from Kara-Oy to Song-Kol over the pass is 45.6 km. From the north — the summer yurt camps on the south shore of Song-Kol.
elev: 3346 m (quad-offroad.com, OunTravela, Asia for Adventure, TripAdvisor). Other values: 3243 m (Baibol Travel), 3201 m (Trip to Kyrgyzstan) — probably intermediate points of the switchbacks.
short: The most “switchbacked” pass to Song-Kol (3346 m): 9 hairpins above the Kurtka River canyon and a height difference of about 800 m over 11 km.
desc: Moldo-Ashuu is a pass in the Moldo-Too range on the southern approach to Lake Song-Kol from Ak-Talaa District. The gravel road climbs out of the Kurtka River canyon in nine hairpin switchbacks (Baibol describes a “seven-level serpentine”) — about 800 m of elevation difference over 11 km from the first bend (OunTravela). On the sides are slopes with tall Tian Shan spruces, flowering valleys, and snowy peaks in the distance. The pass is often shrouded in cloud and thick fog. Of the four road passes to Song-Kol it is considered the most picturesque and the most winding; the road is well kept, but slippery on the steep sections. From November to March it is almost impassable because of snow and fog.
guide: Drive Moldo-Ashuu in at least one direction — it is the most photogenic switchback on the way to Song-Kol. The best shot is from above, from the viewing area by the saddle, when all the hairpins above the Kurtka canyon are visible; climb before noon, while the fog hasn't covered the slopes. Descend in a low gear: the gravel on the steep bends is loose, and trucks and flocks may be coming the other way. Combine it with Kara-Keche or Kalmak-Ashuu to make a loop through the lake. On the descent to Song-Kol, yurts stand by the road in summer — you can have some kumis.
see: The switchback of 9 hairpins above the Kurtka River canyon (a view from above); spruce slopes and the snowy peaks of the Moldo-Too; on the north side — a panorama of the Song-Kol basin and the yurt camps of the south shore.
skip: You're afraid of heights and sharp bends without guardrails. You're driving to Song-Kol from Kochkor and aren't planning a loop — Kalmak-Ashuu is simpler and closer. It's November — March or the forecast is for fog — you won't see anything, and the road is dangerous.
diff: Moderate for a driver: a well-kept gravel road suitable for almost all cars in dry weather (OunTravela), but 9 steep hairpins, a ~800 m height difference over 11 km, fog; Asia for Adventure and Kyrgyz Guide recommend only a 4×4. For cyclists — a hard, slippery climb.
when: June — September. Until June the passes to Song-Kol are blocked by snow (OunTravela); from November to March it is almost impassable (Asia for Adventure, quad-offroad). Snow is possible in summer too (TripAdvisor).
hours: An open road with no barriers or fees; there is no official schedule, winter closure depends on actual snow (November — March, sometimes until late May).
daytime: Morning — before noon: fewer clouds and less fog, good side lighting on the switchback; in the afternoon there is often fog and thunderstorms.
how: From the south — from Ak-Talaa District (Baetov) through the valley and canyon of the Kurtka River, then up the switchbacks to the pass and down to the south shore of Song-Kol; the Kara-Oy — Song-Kol stretch is about 45.6 km (Asia for Adventure, 2024). From Naryn — through Ak-Talaa District; from Kochkor it makes more sense to take Kalmak-Ashuu and use Moldo-Ashuu for the exit toward Naryn/Kazarman. Specific distances from Naryn/Bishkek are not confirmed in the sources.
needcar: Yes: an SUV/crossover with high ground clearance (a 4×4 is recommended); there is no public transport over the pass. A bicycle is possible (Baibol cycling tours).
self: Yes, in your own car with high clearance in dry weather; no permits. For those new to mountain driving, better with a local driver (steep hairpins without guardrails, fog).
roadtype: Gravel dirt road, “well maintained” (OunTravela, quad-offroad), with no asphalt; 9 steep hairpins along the Kurtka canyon; loose gravel on the bends, slippery in rain.
traveltime: The Kara-Oy — Song-Kol stretch (45.6 km) — roughly 1.5–2 h (a calculation from the length and character of the road). The 11 km climb up the switchbacks — 30–40 min. Full times from Naryn/Bishkek were not found in the sources.
stay: There is no lodging at the pass. The nearest is the yurt camps on the south shore of Song-Kol (budget $10–25/person with meals, Caravanistan/visitkyrgyzstan 2025–2026); yurts by the road on the descent in summer (TripAdvisor). In Ak-Talaa District and Naryn — guesthouses (via CBT Naryn). Specific names near the pass are not confirmed.
net: There is mobile signal at the saddle (TripAdvisor, a 2019–2020 review; operator not specified). In the Kurtka canyon and on the shore of Song-Kol — unstable or none.
entry: Free: no source mentions any toll.
transfer: No published transfer prices over Moldo-Ashuu were found. A guideline: a jeep Kochkor — Song-Kol 2500–3500 som per car; a marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn 600 som (May 2026).
bring: Warm clothes and a rain jacket (fog, snow in summer), a spare wheel and a full tank, water and a snack, cash, offline maps; a camera/drone for the view of the switchback.
warn: Steep hairpins without guardrails; thick fog can suddenly cut visibility to almost zero (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). November — March almost impassable; snow is possible in summer too. Altitude 3346 m. Oncoming trucks and flocks on narrow bends.
food: In the summer yurts by the road on the descent to Song-Kol — kumis, tea with boorsok (TripAdvisor); in the Song-Kol camps — beshbarmak, kaimak. Specific places not checked.
reviews: Google Maps: 5/5, 61 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor (Moldo-Ashu Pass): 4.3/5, 10 reviews (July 2015 — February 2020; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: one of the most beautiful passes in the country, views of the switchback, many viewpoints. Cons: altitude, weather (snow even in summer), poor signage.
p.sum: Moldo-Ashuu (3346 m) is the southern exit from Song-Kol toward Naryn, Baetov and Kazarman: 9 hairpins above the Kurtka canyon, a good gravel road, the Kara-Oy — Song-Kol stretch ≈46 km. Drive a crossover/4×4 from June (it is sometimes closed in the first half of June) to September. It makes the most sense to enter Song-Kol via Kalmak-Ashuu from Kochkor and leave via Moldo-Ashuu to the south — to Naryn (Salkyn-Tor, Tash-Rabat) or to Kazarman (≈8 h). There is no lodging at the pass — spend the night in the camps on the south shore.
p.apps.0.title: From the south: Naryn → Ak-Talaa District (Baetov/Kara-Oy/Kurtka) → Moldo-Ashuu
p.apps.0.from: Naryn (the Naryn — Baetov road is 120 km)
p.apps.0.route: Naryn → west along the road to Baetov → Kurtka (the Naryn/Baetov/Kazarman fork) → Kara-Oy → the Kurtka canyon → switchbacks (≈11 km, 9 hairpins) → pass → south shore of Song-Kol
p.apps.0.km: Kara-Oy → Song-Kol 45.6 km; Naryn → Baetov 120 km
p.apps.0.surface: A well-maintained gravel road with no asphalt; loose gravel on bends, slippery in rain; the Naryn — Baetov road was partly paved in 2025
p.apps.0.vehicle: crossover / 4×4 (a sedan — only in dry weather and with experience)
p.apps.0.season: June — September; may be closed in the first half of June; closed for weather on 2 November (2022); November — March practically impassable
p.apps.0.last: Naryn — the last fuel stations, ATMs, shops; in Baetov — shops. There is mobile signal at the saddle (a review), none in the canyon or at the lake
p.apps.0.parking.d: Photo areas at the saddle, free
p.apps.0.trail.d: Kurtka — the start of 2–3-day horse routes to Song-Kol
p.apps.0.haz: Fog down to zero visibility, steep hairpins without guardrails, oncoming trucks (hauling coal) and flocks
p.apps.1.title: From the north: from Song-Kol south (to Kazarman/Naryn)
p.apps.1.route: South shore → a gentle climb across the jailoo (summer pasture) → pass → switchbacks down → Kara-Oy; then west via Ak-Tal and the Kara-Koo pass to Kazarman or east to Naryn
p.apps.1.surface: From the north the climb is gentle; dusty; few villages and cafes on the route
p.apps.1.vehicle: crossover / 4×4; popular with cyclists (Silk Road Mountain Race)
p.apps.1.last: There are no services at Song-Kol — fill up in Kochkor before entering
p.apps.1.haz: Few landmarks and signs, GPS maps are inaccurate in places — use offline tracks
p.transport.2.details: There is no public transport over the pass
p.transport.2.price: not published; a guideline is a jeep Kochkor — Song-Kol ≈5200 som/car (2026)
p.transport.3.provider: Kurtka horse handlers (via Nomad's Land / CBT Naryn)
p.transport.4.details: The switchbacks are hard for a bicycle, otherwise not difficult
p.onsite.horses.0.where: Camps on the south shore of Song-Kol
p.onsite.other.0.details: A view from above of the “seven levels” of switchbacks above the Kurtka canyon; often in cloud
p.onsite.camping: It's windy at the saddle; it's better to pitch a tent lower down — on the jailoo (summer pasture) of the south shore of Song-Kol or in the Kurtka valley.
p.onsite.photo_spots: The upper hairpins of the switchbacks (a view down onto the canyon), the north side — a panorama of the Song-Kol basin.
p.stays.0.name: Yurt camps of the south shore (SonKol-Land Mirlan and others)
p.stays.1.name: Naryn guesthouses (via CBT Naryn)
p.food.0.name: Picnic
p.food.0.details: There are few villages and cafes on the Song-Kol — Ak-Tal — Kazarman road; bring food with you
p.svc.mobile: Signal at the saddle; none in the canyon
p.iti.0.title: Through route Kochkor → Song-Kol → Naryn
p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: Kochkor → Kalmak-Ashuu → Song-Kol (night). Day 2: along the shore south → Moldo-Ashuu → Kara-Oy/Kurtka → Naryn (evening), the next day Salkyn-Tor and Tash-Rabat.
p.iti.1.title: Song-Kol → Kazarman
p.iti.1.plan: An early start, ≈8 h via Moldo-Ashuu, Ak-Tal and Kara-Koo; then Jalal-Abad/Osh (the walnut forests of Arslanbob).
p.season: June: may be closed in the first half. July — September: optimal. October: snow, the first closures. November — March: practically impassable.
p.budget.economy: Naryn: a marshrutka (minibus) 600 som from Bishkek; then only a car (price on request from CBT Naryn) + a yurt 1000–2000 som.
p.budget.comfort: A car with a driver/jeep tour around the Song-Kol loop: €120–$650 for 2 days.
p.access: Only by car; the switchbacks can make children carsick; for wheelchair users — viewing from the car.
